summary: self-certificates ships a PEM-disguised remote code loader that executes attacker Python payload
details: The package advertises in-memory self-signed certificate generation, but index.js contains a hidden loader that reads sample/cert.pem, strips the PEM armor, base64-decodes the body, and passes it to eval(). The decoded JavaScript fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php (the URL itself concealed as a second base64 literal to blend with an OS-update host name) and pipes the response into a detached, window-hidden python3/python interpreter via stdin, executing attacker-controlled code on the installer's host. The loader fires whenever a consumer requires the module and calls the exported generateCertificates() API. The double-layer base64 encoding, PEM-file disguise, and detached/hidden process spawn are consistent with deliberate evasion rather than any legitimate certificate-generation behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
